title: Parti Québécois promises to abolish time change, starting next year
summary: The PQ intends to table a bill in the coming months, and hear from experts in a parliamentary committee.

image.caption: The Parti Québécois hopes to table a bill that would abolish the time change by spring 2027. (Daniel Thomas/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: The PQ intend to table a bill in the coming months, and hear from experts in a parliamentary committee.
Quebecers will wind back the clocks for the final time this year, if future PQ bill passes
Quebecers will turn back their clocks for the last time this weekend, according to the Parti Québécois (PQ). The party hopes to table a bill in the coming months to abolish the time change.

"To all the parents who will be dealing with their children's reactions this time change in the several weeks to come: this is probably the last year we'll be imposing such unnecessary constraints on ourselves," wrote the premier on Facebook.
On the campaign trail, St-Pierre Plamondon had said if elected, he would be open to abolishing the time change as the PQ believed the practice to be counterproductive to health.

items: As other provinces move to abolish seasonal time change, where does Quebec stand?

blocks.text: An online public consultation launched in 2024 by the Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ) government found that 90 per cent of Quebecers who participated were in favour of ditching the time change.

The CAQ did not move forward with the change. In spring of 2025, the former justice minister Simon Jolin-Barrette stated that further consultation would be needed given a change in Quebec's economic situation.

"Several concerns — such as the opinions of experts and scientists, as well as the possibility of aligning with neighbouring states — have been raised through the consultation," wrote Jolin-Barrette in a statement.

items: Time zones in Canada are getting complicated. These maps lay them out
Ontario to move permanently to daylight saving time as long as Quebec, New York follow

blocks.text: B.C., Alberta, the Northwest Territories and Manitoba have all decided to stop switching between daylight and standard time in the last year or so, while residents in Yukon and Saskatchewan haven't wound back their clocks in years.
In 2020, Ontario passed a law that said it would end its time change practice, but only if Quebec and New York did the same.
A PQ spokesperson told CBC that the party plans to hear from experts during a parliamentary committee hearing on adopting permanent daylight time or standard time.
The former offers more light in the evening, and the latter in the morning.

Jacqueline is a reporter from Toronto, now happily living in Montreal. She loves to report on all stories, but has a special interest in emergency management and climate. You can reach out to her with a story tip at jacqueline.newsome@cbc.ca.
